primitives.name: Abstract Conditions Axiom
primitives.verbatim_quote: The abstract conditions first enumerated in chapter III represented in part divergencies in degree only from real life, and were in part arbitrary abstractions from fundamental characteristics of the pecuniary organization made for the purpose of a separate study of the constituent elements.
primitives.assumptions: Conditions are idealized representations; real-world deviations are quantifiable perturbations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When deviation exceeds threshold of measurable impact on systemic behavior.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic model of market structure where abstract conditions define prior distributions over realizable economic configurations.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation metrics from empirical data against theoretical baseline.

primitives.name: Uncertainty Grouping Principle
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the uncertainty in a particular case is measurable, it may in effect be eliminated by the grouping or clubbing of a sufficient number of cases to secure certainty in regard to the group.
primitives.assumptions: Grouping reduces variance via law of large numbers; measurable uncertainty implies statistical regularity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When individual case variability exceeds collective stability thresholds.

layer2.mapping: Underpins GSE's ensemble forecasting framework where grouped stochastic processes yield deterministic outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Variance reduction ratio across grouped scenarios versus individual event predictions.
